hook.line: "You should absolutely have a second website."
hook.visual: Handheld selfie while walking outside in low sun; orange boxed title 'Why You Should Have a Second Website in 2026' at the top, big word captions with orange highlight below.

beats.what: Flat yes-answer to the caption's question, with the 'why' title box at the top.
Cut: defines the idea, a resource site in your industry not tied to your brand.
Social proof: four clients already doing it, a fifth starting now.
Reason: one more place to post blog posts, and as a third party it carries more weight.
Key line: it carries more weight with the AI, which now makes the recommendations.
Cut to 'so how do you do it?': the turn from why to how.
Expectation setting: a long-term play, no results in the first three months.
Step: pick an exact-match domain, and why it still helps.
Step: you need two things, content and links; start with free foundational links.
Step: write helpful answers first and don't recommend your brand until it ranks.

why_it_works: Contrarian, specific idea (a second, unbranded website) that the SEO viewer has not heard, so the 'why' title creates a curiosity gap.
Why-then-how structure with an explicit pivot line at 53 s gives a second reason to keep watching halfway through.
Ties an old SEO tactic to the new worry (AI recommendations), so it feels current for 2026.
Walking selfie in daylight reads as an unscripted expert tip, not a produced ad.
weaknesses: 132 s with a 36.9 s longest shot and almost no visuals beyond captions; retention leans fully on the words.
No call to action; the video ends mid-thought.
Captions sit outside the safe area the whole time (measured outside_safe_share 1.0).
for_robert: Use the explicit 'so how do you do it?' pivot halfway through a why-then-how reel. That line is the right moment for Fred to swim in with a checklist, giving the second half a fresh visual start.
